name: Sengled Smart LED Multicolor A19 Zigbee (US)

radios.note: Zigbee only; Sengled sells this bulb as 'Hub Required'.

matter.note: Zigbee-only bulb. Sengled's Matter bulb is a separate Wi-Fi model.

apple_home.note: Sengled does not list Apple Home for this bulb; no official source either way.

google_home.note: Google Assistant works through the Sengled hub and Sengled Home cloud. Google Home speakers are not Zigbee hubs. Sengled's cloud had outages in 2025.

alexa.note: Pairs directly with Echo models that have a Zigbee hub. Amazon removed the Sengled Alexa skill on 1 Aug 2025, so the Sengled-hub route to Alexa no longer works.

smartthings.note: Sengled lists the SmartThings hub as compatible and documents pairing.

home_assistant.note: No official Home Assistant or Sengled source names this bulb; a generic Zigbee coordinator likely works but is unconfirmed.

hubRequired.note: For bulbs, this means needing a bridge or hub for basic app control. This Zigbee bulb needs a Sengled hub, SmartThings hub or Zigbee Echo.

localControl.note: No official source describes local control. The Sengled app path depends on Sengled's cloud; third-party Zigbee hubs may differ.

summary: The Sengled Smart LED Multicolor A19 (E11-N1EAW) is a US Zigbee colour bulb with an E26 base, rated at 800 lumens. It needs a Zigbee hub: a Sengled Smart Hub, a SmartThings hub or an Echo with a built-in Zigbee hub. Amazon removed the Sengled Alexa skill in August 2025 after repeated outages, so Alexa control now means pairing the bulb directly to a Zigbee Echo.
caveats: Requires a Zigbee hub; it has no Wi-Fi or Bluetooth.
Sengled's cloud had extended outages in mid-2025 and Amazon pulled the Sengled Alexa skill on 1 August 2025. We found no official Sengled statement on service status.
Sengled says these bulbs should not be used on dimmer switches.
